sourceLocation.description: gatewayValidationHeaders ranks the ambient process.env[apiKeyEnvKey] ahead of the plan's ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, even when plan.env owns apiKeyEnvKey with a deliberately blank value.

candidates.finding: A plan that deliberately blanks its provider key (plan.env[apiKeyEnvKey]='') still falls through to the ambient shell value before the plan's ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, so validation can authenticate with a credential the child never sees (the child runs with { ...process.env, ...plan.env }, where the blank plan value overrides the ambient one).
candidates.impact: Gateway provider validation can use a different token than the spawned child, so validation may pass or fail against the wrong credential when a config supplies an auth token instead of a provider API key.
candidates.whyDeferred: gatewayValidationHeaders is pre-existing and untouched by AI-3109 — this PR only made the gateway-routing test hermetic against a leaked ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; changing header precedence is outside the reserved-exit-codes scope.
candidates.dedupeHint: gatewayValidationHeaders blank plan key vs ambient env precedence
candidates.suggestedTitle: Treat a deliberately-blank plan provider key as authoritative in gatewayValidationHeaders
acceptanceCriteria: When plan.env owns apiKeyEnvKey with a blank value, gatewayValidationHeaders skips the ambient process.env fallback and uses the plan's ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
A gateway-routing test can keep an ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set and still resolve validation auth to the plan's auth token.
